results.failing_first: Before the implementation, concurrent same-key lookups caused two HTTP requests; the shared-request assertion failed.

behavior: Least recently used eviction meets entry and charged-byte limits. Oversized successful results bypass caching. Expiry is lazy.
Only successful parsed schemas and typed 404 errors are memoized. Other failures remain errors for all coalesced waiters and do not populate the cache.
Clones share one credential-scoped cache; separately constructed clients remain isolated. Same-key requests share a caller-owned flight, unrelated keys proceed without a network lock.
Owner cancellation closes its request and wakes followers for read-only takeover within their original deadlines. Follower cancellation preserves the owner. No background library tasks.
Subject limits apply before key/path allocation and I/O; incoming reference count and subjects are checked before cache admission. Diagnostics expose aggregate counts without subject labels.

References are resolved one level, preserving order and duplicates; cyclic declarations do not recurse. One overall batch request_timeout includes all waits/retries. Earlier individually successful entries may remain cached when a later batch member fails.
limits: Deterministic owned loopback HTTP tests and existing TLS tests; no live Schema Registry or external authentication service is claimed.
Charged retained bytes include capacities and inline entry/Arc storage, not hash-bucket/allocator overhead, process RSS or caller-owned result clones/futures; applications must bound callers/results.
Paused Tokio clocks are advanced only after fixture barriers to prove freshness and the overall reference deadline. The active-slot deadline test uses a bounded real-time window.

No new dependency families, root dependency changes or default features. Tokio sync is enabled for the optional registry implementation; test-util is a dev-only feature. The existing Ring backend needs a C compiler.
Current root CI does not exercise this workspace-excluded companion; the recorded companion checks are local stable/MSRV runs.
